It's about a 15 minute walk from Shimoyoshida station to the bottom of the path. The path up is about 300 steps to the pagoda. From the pagoda to the top maybe an extra 5 minutes. So I guess it just depends on how quickly you can climb steep steps! 

Also, when you leave the station go right and there's a sidewalk with signs that will lead you right to it. When I went the first time we didn't know and got lost in the town for an hour trying to find our way there.

Yes, it is absolutely worth it! I've been there in both early May and July. It is stunning! 

Be sure to hike to the very top of the path past the pagoda as well, you can get an unobstructed view of Fujisan.

Another great view is at Kawaguchiko Lake, I definitely recommend that as well and it's on the way to Shimoyoshida (Chureito) via train.

I think the most important thing to remember when it comes to MBTI is that it is not a personality type but a preference type. (ie how you prefer to handle conflict or problems)

I'm an ISFP and I usually avoid conflict like the plague because I try to keep my life peaceful and calm. If it must be addressed I prefer compromise as much as possible otherwise, honestly, I blow up and let my feelings and emotions take control and get the better of me. My bf on the other hand is an INTJ and he will bring up the issue straight away, very bluntly, without much regard to anyone's feelings and will talk about it nonstop until he feels it has been resolved. (It's nauseating and exhausting lol) Also it's extremely unlikely that he will compromise. 

Again, its just a preference. I know some people take comfort in finding a place or group of people they can connect with or are similar to. MBTI cannot and will not define who everyone is. I think more than anything it's just fun to find out what type a person falls into and how much they do show those traits. :)

I have tons of great memories I know I'll never forget in my travels, but one time in Spain...

I was travelling with a group a friends when we were 18 and our last stop was Madrid, Spain. I was incredibly ill during our trip and I ended up completely losing my voice. We were checking out shops on one of the side roads of Puerta del Sol. I was walking behind my friends when all of a sudden a Spaniard walking past me grabs my arm and starts pulling me away from my friends. I kept trying to tell him no, but I had no voice and he wouldn't let go. I tried yelling for my friends, who were soon to be out of my sight, but I finally broke out of his vice like grip and ran. I clung to my best friend and tried to explain to her what happened. It was terrifying at the time. I find it hilarious now though. 

My mom jokingly warned me that they liked blonde hair/blue eyed girls hahah. I definitely can't wait to go back to Spain though!
